native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest-growth century between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is 1400 BCE, identified by the largest mean pollen_grate_100 (≈+0.193 %/yr), the largest single-year spike (≈+0.46 % at CE ≈ −1415 BCE) and the largest contemporaneous mean of g_all_mean (+0.00284). The strongest sustained high-growth phase is the contiguous pair **1300 BCE – 1400 BCE**, the only consecutive centuries in which both pollen_grate_100 and g_all_mean are jointly positive (1300 BCE: +0.00111 / +0.00142; 1400 BCE: +0.00193 / +0.00284). The capital.csv 12-capital Zmean composite independently peaks at 1400 BCE (+0.94) and falls to +0.26 in 1500 BCE, directionally confirming the call without overriding the pollen/KDE evidence. Under the alternative C2 binning (ceil-of-century), the peak label shifts to "1500 BCE" but both conventions identify the same physical ≈100-year span (CE ≈ −1500 to −1400). All numbers come from the _inter / 100-year-smoothed columns, because raw pollen and the raw capital Z values are ~95 % missing in this window.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Loaded the three CSVs (decimal="," for capital.csv). 2. Filtered time_series_data to CE ∈ [−2000, −1100] and dropped the 1-row "century-20" bin. 3. Aggregated nine complete centuries (1900–1100 BCE) by mean pollen_grate_100, mean g_all_mean and net Δ pollen_inter. 4. Ranked centuries — clear peak at 1400 BCE (mean = 0.001931). 5. Identified the sustained phase as the longest contiguous run above the window-mean pollen_grate_100 of −0.000147: 1300–1400 BCE. 6. Ran a C2 sensitivity check; under C2 the peak label shifts to "1500 BCE", but both labels describe the same physical ~100-y span. 7. Cross-checked with capital.csv 12-capital Zmean — peaks at 1400 BCE (+0.94), directionally aligned.

        "sizeA": num of variables used in HypoA
        "sizeB": num of variables used in HypoB
        "intersection": num of variables common in HypoA and HypoB. Use *fuzzy matching* to determine intersection, accounting for paraphrases or slightly different surface forms
        "explanation": a short text explanation about the variables
        }}```
        Answer:

score.explanation: HypoA uses time (BCE centuries) and growth, without specifying a growth measure. HypoB uses time (BCE/CE), pollen growth (pollen_grate_100), KDE growth (g_all_mean), and the 12-capital Z-score mean composite. Time is shared directly; unspecified growth in HypoA fuzzily matches the growth measures in HypoB. Means, spikes, and alternative century bins are summaries or representations, not additional variables.
